howToSteps.text: Pour the full recipe batter into a greased 9-inch round pan. It sits at the same depth it had in the square pan.

title: 8-Inch Square to 9-Inch Round Pan
tutorial: This is the only pan swap that needs no maths at all. An 8-inch square covers 64 square inches and a 9-inch round covers 63.6. The difference is 0.4 square inches, less than 1 percent, which no recipe can tell apart. King Arthur Baking says the two pans can be substituted for one another in any recipe, and that is the whole guidance.

Both pans hold the same batter, too. An 8-inch square holds 8 cups to the rim and a 9-inch round holds 8 cups, and both hold about 8.8 cups by straight-wall geometry at 2 inches deep. Fill either pan half to two-thirds full, which is about 5.3 cups at most, and the bake is the same in both.

The one real difference is the corners. A square pan has four corners that get heat from two sides and brown first. A round pan has no corners, so the edges bake a touch more evenly all the way around. If your square-pan brownies always come out with dry corners and a soft middle, the round pan fixes that without changing anything else.

Cutting changes, too. A square cake cuts into neat bars. A round cake cuts into wedges, which suits a coffee cake or a snack cake served in slices. For brownies the square pan is still the better shape, because brownie wedges look odd on a plate. For anything served in slices, the round pan is the nicer cut.

Bake at the same temperature and the same time. Same area, same depth, same pan depth, same bake. The toothpick test works the same way in both pans. If you have ever hesitated over this swap, stop hesitating: it is the free one.
